newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended at their lows following losses in New York. December lost $2.30 to close at $315.00 per tonne, while March shed $2.30 to close at $311.80 per tonne. In New York raw sugar futures closed sharply lower with nearby March losing 16 points to close at 10.54 cents/lb. May gave up 12 points to close at 10.59 cents/lb. The outer months lost between 5 and 9 points. Prospects of another surplus in 1996/97 and sluggish offtake weighed on sentiment. Given current fundamentals chances for noticeably higher prices are slim.

CHINA - China imported 132,976 tonnes of sugar, raw value, in September 1996, significantly down on the 360,915 tonnes imported the same month the previous year. Total imports in crop year 1995/96 (September/August) reached 1.945 million tonnes, down from 2.907 million tonnes imported the previous year. Main suppliers of raw sugar in September 1996 were Cuba (29,000 vs 77,068 tonnes) and Australia (84,204 vs 56,000 tonnes). The main white sugar supplier was South Korea with 2,667 tonnes vs 3,634 tonnes. The country exported 102,192 tonnes of sugar in September 1996, up from 32,407 tonnes exported the same month the previous year. Total exports in crop year 1995/96 reached 830,203 tonnes, up from 540,004 tonnes exported in 1994/95. Main markets for Chinese white sugar in September 1996 were Indonesia (13,001 vs 0 tonnes), Pakistan (50,500 vs 0 tonnes) and Saudi Arabia (26,481 vs 13,200 tonnes).

FRANCE - Sugar consumption in June 1996 amounted to 209,166 tonnes raw value, down from last year's 219,364 tonnes. This brought cumulative consumption in the first three quarters of 1995/96 (October/June) up to 1.59 million tonnes, unchanged from last year. Total consumption in 1994/95 was 2.18 million tonnes compared to 2.21 million tonnes in 1993/94.

PORTUGAL - According to revised figures, sugar imports in June 1996 amounted to 12,982 tonnes, raw value, down from last year's 22,676 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first half of 1996 up to 139,759 tonnes against 192,884 tonnes imported in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1995 reached 312,542 tonnes against 340,710 tonnes in 1994. Major countries of origin in January/June 1996 were Swaziland with 32,197 raws against 28,123, Zimbabwe with 19,555 compared to 19,939 tonnes and Jamaica with 18,094 tonnes against nil. Exports in January/June 1996 were negligible (5,451 tonnes).

TURKEY - The Turkish sugar beet crop obviously made good progress in the second half of September. Sugar content on September 30 was 15.9 percent against 15.2 percent in the previous test while beet weight climbed to 50.13 tonnes per ha against 47.97 tonnes on September 15. This resulted in a theoretical sugar weight per ha of 7.97 tonnes, white value against 7.31 tonnes in the previous test. Due to industrial action in 1995 comparable figures for the previous year are not available. Nevertheless the beet tests suggest that the crop is in a rather good shape and Turkey expects to harvest a total of 1.85 million tonnes, white value.
Ethiopia has delayed announcing the winner of the tender to supply 25,000 tonnes of white sugar, official sources said. It was not said when an announcement would be made.
